texts.label: text
texts.orig: The  public  procurement  and  asset  disposal system  in  Kenya  has  undergone  continous transformation  through  the  Government's efforts to ensure that it is  in  tandem with emerging issues in procurement, technological changes and best practices that  uphold  the  principles  of  transparency, accountability,  integrity,  openness,  fairness, competition  and  value  for  money.  A  well functioning  public  procurement  system  is  a catalyst for the realisation of the Vision 2030, Medium Term III and the Big Four Agenda.

texts.orig: The Authority during the period under review implemented a number of activities towards enhancing  the  effeciency  and  effectiveness of the public procurement and asset disposal system.  The  activities  covered  the  areas  of compliance monitoring and enforcement of standards, complaints management, investigations, advisory  services,  research, reporting and stakeholders engagement.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: On compliance monitoring and enforcement of  standards,  the  Authority  undertook  59 procurement  assessments,  4  procurement reviews, 14 contract audits, 46 follow-ups on the implementation of the recommendations from previous assessments, and 2 procurement inspections in procuring entities; to  determnine the level of compliance with the  provisions  of  the  Act,  Regulations  and directives.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Authority receives and resolves complaints raised by the participants in the  public  procurement  and  asset  disposal system. During the year, the Authority resolved 355 of the 488 complaints received.  From  the  analysis  of  the  nature of  the  complaints,  40%  were  on  flaws  in tender evaluation and development of specifications,  21%  of  the  complaints  were on delayed payments, 15% on alleged corrupt practices  during  procurement  proceedings and  9%  on  alleged  irregularities  during  the procurement  process,  among  others.  Some of  the  complaints  were  investigated  and findings shared with the parties and the law enforcement agencies.

texts.orig: At  the  international  scene,  the  Authority convened the 11 th East African Procurement Forum (EAPF) between 28th and 30th November 2018, under the theme, 'Strengthening  Integrity  and  Accountability in Public  Procurement'.  The  Forum  was attended by 226 delegates drawn from the  EAC  member  states,  a  representation from Ghana and development partners. The Authority hosted delegations from the Central Procurement Technical Unit of  Bangladesh  and  Members  of  Uganda Parliamentary Committee on Finance, Planning and Economic Development. texts.text: 1.1 Introduction

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (the Authority) is established under Section 8  (1)  of  the  Public  Procurement  and  Disposal  Act,  2015  (the  Act)  and  is  charged  with monitoring, assessing and reviewing the public procurement and asset disposal system to ensure that they respect the national values and other provisions of the constitution.
texts.text: The Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (the Authority) is established under Section 8  (1)  of  the  Public  Procurement  and  Disposal  Act,  2015  (the  Act)  and  is  charged  with monitoring, assessing and reviewing the public procurement and asset disposal system to ensure that they respect the national values and other provisions of the constitution.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Apart from the Regulatory Board described above, there exists also the Public Administrative Review Board is established under section 27 (1) of the Act. It is a central independent procurement appeals review board that should ensure reasonable access to its services in all parts of the Republic as far as it is appropriate to do so. The Authority provides secretariat and administrative services, and appoints the secretary to the Review Board.

texts.text: STATEMENT OF THE BOARD CHAIRMAN

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Authority is a key player in ensuring accountability and realization of value for money for public funds spent through the public procurement and asset disposal process. The Public Procurement Regulatory Board took reigns at the Authority in November 2018 after the institution having been without a Board for three years and at when there is need to take a bold step and chart a new way of transparency and accountability in public procurement.

The Public Procurement Regulatory Board took reigns at the Authority in November 2018 after the institution having been without a Board for three years and at when there is need to take a bold step and chart a new way of transparency and accountability in public procurement.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Authority operates in a dynamic environment that is always offering new opportunities and challenges. Strategic planning is therefore necessary to enable the Authority exploit the opportunities and mitigate the risks and challenges posed by these changes in its operating environment.
